super fun New Years story: i quit smoking w33d on December 24, been having some pretty nasty withdrawals (loss of appetite, insomnia, extreme irritability) — by far the hardest week of 2021 for me.

Then yesterday on NYE, I got food poisoning (which was odd because all I had was a tiny croissant & a latte in the morning). I threw up 40+ times and spent the evening sweating in bed… AND all the pharmacies were closed so I couldn’t get any medicine. I was so dehydrated that I begged the only emergency ambulance in the city to hook me up to an IV so I could replenish and go out with my friends. They said it wasn’t possible unless they took me to the hospital. Obviously fuck that

In an attempt to initiate the rally of the century, I managed to put on my suit and go to the party for 10 minutes before I realized my fate was sealed. As I walked back home up the cold icy hill defeated and disappointed, I threw up another 5 times in the street. Didn’t miss a stride.

Coincidentally, this is the third New Years in a row where I’ve been deathly ill, so I theorized: perhaps life has made the beginning of the past few years a nightmare for me so I appreciate the remaining 364 days. I consider it an involuntary “reset.” Having been physically and mentally humbled (again), it’s only up from here.

I’m feeling much better today, and I know this year is going to be astronomical for me. I hope you all grab 2022 by the fucking horns and accomplish everything you want

Love Fiercely per me non è solo il motto del mio percorso di essere umano, ma un credo da condividere con tutti e un ideale per il quale battersi. Amare con fierezza, amare come vuoi e chi vuoi è il significato di tutto quello che ha spinto le mie scelte, sempre, tutto quello in cui ho sempre creduto, tutto quello che oggi mi permette di essere la persona innamorata delle della mia vita e di chi la popola. Con la campagna #LoveFiercely che ho voluto in supporto ad @cigarcigaymilano oggi voglio dire a tutti di amare se stessi prima di tutto, perché solo cosí ci si sente liberi di amare come e chi si vuole. Io nella mia vita l’ho fatto, ho amato indipendentemente dal genere, senza farmi costringere dalle etichette che gli altri volevano darmi e lo stesso hanno fatto @loredane_tshilombo e @saralapignola, @nickcerioni e @leandroemede, @mehths e @chiarapierii.  La mia storia e le storie di queste tre coppie che stimo spero possano essere di esempio per tutti , perché amare in maniera pura è sempre la scelta più giusta che ognuno di noi può fare. Grazie a questa iniziativa e ad una mia donazione personale supporteremo il progetto Scuola di @cigarcigaymilano: andremo nelle scuole di Milano e provincia per raccontare queste storie d'amore e sensibilizzare i giovanissimi sulle tematiche del bullismo. Adesso è il tuo turno, raccontami la tua storia di amore fiero taggami e utilizza #LoveFiercely così io possa vederla 💖

Ho riso, ho pianto, ma sopratutto ho imparato molto dalle storie d’amore e di vita di @loredane_tshilombo @saralapignola @mehths @chiarapierii @nickcerioni @leandroemede . Sono loro i protagonisti assoluti dell’iniziativa #LoveFiercely che ho voluto in supporto ad @cigarcigaymilano e che in questo video si raccontano. Sono loro i protagonisti, le voci, le anime belle che spero possano essere d’esempio a noi tutti e simbolo di un cambiamento radicale nella società dove voglio essere orgogliosa di vivere e crescere la mia famiglia. Un grazie speciale anche a @paoloarmelli , lui è stato la guida di questo racconto schietto ed emozionante. Un grazie a tutte le persone del mio team che ogni giorno si battono per portare alla luce progetti come questo @fabiomariadamato filippoinnocenti @luisa_loz @azzurragentile @chiaradadalt @fabionu_ perché il nostro non è solo un lavoro di squadra ma una comunione di valori ❤️

For the most part of my teenage/adult life my biggest physical insecurity has been my skin: I’ve always had breakouts/acne and showing my skin when it was inflammed was very triggering for me. 
In the past 6 years my skin has changed and got so much better: what really helped me was balancing my hormones with inositol (totally natural), live a happier life and not think about it too much. Every once in a while I get breakouts, and It’s totally ok and I made peace with the situation. 
The day we were finally discharged from the hospital I had a very bad rash on the right part of my chin: I blame it on my hormones + obviously super high stress level. I could have avoided talking about it and showing it but then I was thinking.. Why should I not talk about it? We have to normalize bad skin days too, and not having the pressure to ever feel perfect 🙏🏻

I woke up one morning and decided — I deserve to feel good in red.

The reason I always hated red, was because it’s the color that people will always look at. And I didn’t want anyone to look at me. I felt so ashamed of my body and my appearance - why would I want to make it stand out more?

So I never wore red. Ever. In fact I developed a hatred for the color. Makeup. Clothes. Accessories. All of it.

I mean — if you buy a red car your car insurance literally goes up. I had such negative feelings towards the color for so long.

But recently I woke up one morning and said… why the fuck? What the fuck? Who the fuck? 😂 And in that moment.. I stopped hating red. 

I may still feel a bit uncomfortable in red clothes and makeup. But there’s something really special about when I build up the courage to actually wear it.

Bringing color back into my life one outfit at a time. ❤️

After parent teacher conferences the year I was 14, my mom came out to the car where I was waiting. She was upset, and she yelled at me which she rarely ever did. My teachers had told her that I was in my own world and not paying attention in class. I asked her why she was so upset. She said because all she ever wanted was for me to have more than she did. She said she wanted me to be better. To be stronger and smarter and have options and have whatever it is I wanted from this life. She told me when I was born she was so happy it was me, that I was a girl, because she wanted me to be great. My mom was the first person in her family to go to college. She moved to london knowing not a soul with a new baby because she wanted  to give me opportunities that she didn’t have. She gave up her job - that she loved & that was a huge sense of pride - to take care of me. She drove me to rehearsals and helped me with my homework and said “no, just apply to Stanford you never know”! She knew immediately when a boyfriend was bad news but didn’t judge me when I wasn’t ready to break up. She supported me through chaotic cross country moves and random job changes. She held me up while I went through the darkest times of my life. She made choices and sacrifices to give me a better shot. Mom, you are great. I love you. I am who I am because of you 🤍

Qualche giorno fa la senatrice Liliana Segre mi ha portato alla scoperta di un luogo del quale non conoscevo nulla, il memoriale della Shoah a Milano. Ascoltare dalla voce di Liliana, come dice lei “da nonna a nipote”, la storia di chi è stato perseguitato in questo luogo a pochi passi da casa mi ha fatto soffrire e soprattutto riflettere. Ho capito quanto le persecuzioni che spesso pensiamo siano lontane da noi nel tempo e nella geografia, si siano invece consumate sotto casa nostra, sotto gli occhi indifferenti di molti nostri concittadini. In questo luogo ho imparato quanto restare indifferenti all’odio e alla violenza, sia a suo modo un gesto ulteriore di violenza e odio. Oggi voglio condividere questa mia esperienza invitando tutti a visitare il @MemorialeDellaShoah a Milano (in Stazione Centrale) per vedere, pensare, agire. Grazie a Liliana che da donna a donna mi ha dato una lezione di vita, di umanità e di attivismo. Diciamo no all’indifferenza.
🇬🇧 
A few days ago the Italian Senator Liliana Segre invited me to visit with her a very special place I have never been to, the Shoah Memorial in Milan. Listening to Liliana’s story, which she narrated from “grandma to niece” like she said to me, was extremely touching. It made me suffer and also think a lot. It made me realize how persecutions, which we often think are so far away from us both in time and space, were happening in our cities under the indifferent eyes of many people. In this place I learnt how being indifferent to hate and violence is actually a way of perpetuating hate and violence. Today I want to share my experience with you and I want to invite you to visit the @memorialedellashoah in Milan (inside Milan's Central Station) to see, think and take action. 
Thank you to Liliana who, from one woman to another, today gave me a lesson on life, humanity and activism. Let’s say no to indifference.

I was on every dating app under the sun trying to find some sort of connection to heal my pain, but after many failed dates and interactions, I decided a connection cannot be forced and I gave up. As I went to delete the Tinder app after several months of trying, I saw Cody’s big bold smile pop up on the homepage, and it was absolutely infectious. 

So I swiped right. We began talking everyday and eventually we decided to go on a date. I have never been one to believe in love at first sight, but that is what I felt with Cody. The most immediate connection I’ve ever felt in my life. 

While I often show Cody on my socials, I have never truly been able to express what he has done for me. Cody taught me that love is real. Love is powerful, beautiful, and I am deserving of it.

I am a very closed off person, someone who struggles to share their emotions and be vulnerable. But Cody taught me that it’s okay to cry, it’s okay to speak your mind, and you’re never “weak” for showing your raw emotions. You are STRONG.

Cody has helped me navigate my mental health struggles, my eating disorder, and this fast paced career. He has loved me every single day even when I can be an absolute raging bitch, haha. 

Cody is kind, compassionate, hardworking, lovable, intelligent, tenacious, goofy, mature, resilient, and much more. I hope for everyone to have a Cody in their life!

Cody is truly one of a kind, and for that, this collection is dedicated to him. I love you Cody. 💚

Obviously I am extremely dramatic but I’m not being funny when I say that on the first day of hiking, I thought I was gonna have to sit out all of the hikes because I was so weak. I had this moment where I was alone on the hike and I just started crying because I felt so crappy and useless. 

I wanted to come on @theranchmalibu because I wanted to push myself really, really hard at something that I’m not good at (hiking). I wanted to get out of my comfort zone and also be in my physical body which is something I find really difficult as an anxious/in-my-head person. 

So anyway I pushed through and the second day I did better and by the third day - classic me - I have done a 180 and am now obsessed with the hikes. They are HARD, don’t get me wrong. But it’s one foot in front of the other, kind of like in life. Today I literally had to take 2 steps and stop and dry heave it was so steep. But I made it. One baby step at a time. And by trying to get out of my head I’m actually working through a lot of shit that won’t leave my head (more on that later). Walking with your own thoughts is scary but beautiful. So this is my long way of saying that sometimes it’s just about putting one foot infront of the other when things feel impossible.

Living Hell is a story about my childhood. It’s a story about how I struggled growing up inside a real-life living hell in a tiny room in the Philippines. My whole life, I’ve been trying to escape my childhood trauma, my living hell, and no matter how much therapy I do, no matter how much medicine I take, and no matter how far I try to run away…it always comes back to haunt me. The music video is inspired by my childhood room. My room was yellow and had a lock on the outside. Yellow because it was a color I was forced to like growing up. It was my parents way of letting me know that they have the power in the house. And a lock on the outside because my parents wanted to make sure that I didn’t escape when I was in there. It was really hard for me to relive this while shooting the music video. I really want to talk to you more about it when I’m ready. Sorry for the essay the reason I’m writing this is because I want all of you who are reading this and all of you who have supported me along this journey to understand that I love you more than you know. You guys are my escape. You guys are why I wake up everyday. You guys are the reason that I’m able to break free from this mess and in my darkest times, understand that things are going to be okay. I truly can’t thank you enough and I want you to know that I’m here for you the same way that you’re here for me. To anyone who is also going through their own living hell, you will escape and I'll be right there by your side. This one's for you💛

#99 ORIGINALS
The last Polaroid of my @99Originals photography project, taken in Zero Gravity. I wrote this on the last day of our journey:

“Day 99… how can I come down from a lifetime of memories made in the last 3 months? I’ve travelled a quarter million miles, shared moments with characters that only exist in movies, uncontrollably wept, hideously laughed, shattered my dominant hand, became addicted to weed, alcohol, and quick thrills, all while surviving a creative mania that may have yielded my Magnum Opus.

I’m not sure I’ll ever ‘come down’ from this.
I’m not sure I want to.

I’m so tired. Physically and mentally drained. But so FULL.

It ended just as quickly as it started, and I’ve had no time to process. Now comes the hard part: how will I break my bad habits, but keep the good ones? Perhaps my therapist can help with this.

I’m so happy we documented this journey. There are simply too many memories for the brain alone to remember. I get emotional when I look back at the Polaroids. I get sent back to each moment, vividly. Now, they will live forever. 

I hope I inspire people to do more.
I hope I inspire people to do what they can’t.

Life is so VAST. And GRAND. And beautiful.

I want to live it all. I think I will.”

One of the most frequently asked questions that I receive from women is how to not be afraid to turn 30. The question always makes me so sad because it reflects the limiting belief that so many women have - that aging is scary and bad and shameful. I often say how I feel my life began at 29. It’s when I found my career, it’s when I started to feel truly confident, and it’s when I feel like I started to live authentically. Now at 32 I am happier, more confident and more proud of my career than I ever have been. Getting older is beautiful. My birthday wish is that you all rid yourselves of limiting beliefs - about age, about your looks, about whatever is holding you back. You all have so much potential and I hope I inspire you to reach it. Thank you for letting me into your lives for the past year. I can’t wait for the next one. I love growing up with you 🤍🤍🤍🤍

Today was amazing. Every time I get to meet you guys in person, it’s amazing. The last couple of days have been a little rough with negative comments and dumb online bullshit and sometimes I feel like I’m alone in my house with my phone just speaking into a void. 

And then, when I’m lucky…

I get to put my phone down and meet you guys and hug you and hear your stories and hear about how we share and connect on certain aspects of life. I get to hear how you listen to my podcast on your runs, how you just left a toxic relationship, how you worked up the courage to leave a shitty job, how you’ve shifted your perspective on things, how you’ve been following me since I crashed the mini Cooper. I get to meet you who come together as best friends. As roommates. As sisters, as moms, and as daughters. I get to FaceTime your friends who couldn’t come because they’re cramming for a final. I get to read your letters. I get to pet your dogs and wave to your HBOTs and even say hello to the tiny humans you grew inside your bodies. And suddenly I feel like I’m living in technicolor. 

You all mean more to me than you’ll ever know. I feel your love and I’m beaming it right back. Forever 🤍

As the years go by, I have a deeper appreciation for my body, and that in order to make the right decisions for my body, knowledge truly is power. In 2023, it’s going to be increasingly important that we ALL share knowledge because the more we know, the stronger we are. I’ve been very vocal about my decision to get off hormonal birth control and I’ve gotten a lot of questions around what I use to prevent pregnancy so I wanted to share that I use @naturalcycles and explain a little bit more about how it works as it is a newer birth control option.
 
Natural Cycles is the first and only FDA cleared birth control app. The app is powered by a smart algorithm that uses my body temp to confirm my daily fertility status - so it tells me each day if I can get pregnant that day or not. It’s able to tell me this because there are small but significant shifts in a woman’s body temp during her cycle, and the NC algorithm is able to identify these shifts to pinpoint where I am in my cycle. This is important because there are only 6 days every cycle that a woman can get pregnant. I know I wasn’t taught a lot about this and it’s been pretty mind blowing to not only learn about reproductive health in general but to feel the empowerment that comes with more knowledge. Birth control is such a personal decision and everyone has their own needs and wants. I’m happy I found a non-hormonal option that works for me.
 
If you’re interested in learning more, you can go to Naturalcycles.com to find out if Natural Cycles is right for you. And if you use my code TINX or go to naturalcycles.com/tinx you’ll also get 20% off an annual subscription + a free thermometer. I use my @ouraring to measure (it syncs automatically to the NC° app) but the thermometer is another great option.
 
p.s. NC is for 18+ and does not protect against STIs *ad

10 books that stuck with me this year: 
1. Olive (this was recommended to me by my friend Jyoti. It’s an unbelievable novel that perfectly encapsulates the splintering era of female friendships and offers advice on how to survive it. Deep discussion of motherhood, relationships, feminism, fertility and modern womanhood. It made me feel at once relieved to know that girl gangs all over the world are going through the same thing in their late 20s early 30s. But it also made me so desperately sad to realize well, just that. ) 
2. Tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow (this book ripped me in two. Recommended by my friend Charlotte it’s basically a little life lite in the sense that you will be so involved with the characters and their lives you’ll feel like a real friend moved away when the book is done. Unbelievably written with prose so rich you’ll feel like you’re gently being rocked like a baby when you read it. And speaking of babies - you’ll cry like one several times in the book. )
3. The obstacle is the way (recommended by someone who was a stranger at the time, but became a friend. When I was going through a hard time, this person reached out and recommended that I read this book and it really helped me see things in a new light. It’s practical and one of those books that helps you feel stable. Lots of actionable tips and I’m so grateful to the person who recommend this book to me.) 
4. Detransition baby (an incredibly beautiful window into the trans experience. Stunningly written with so much empathy and nuance, the novel invites you to walk in shoes you may never have considered. )
5. Taste (I mean, how could this book be bad. As someone who has been obsessed with food and cooking, and how food and cooking can bring people together this felt biblical to read. A life through food. Love through food. Loss through food. So thoughtfully complied and written. This book confirmed to me that I am a person who will see the world through food for the rest of my life. And I feel so lucky to be one of those people.

Il vestito manifesto:

Quando abbiamo iniziato a pensare agli abiti per le due serate di @Sanremorai abbiamo subito capito di non volere vestiti solo perché eccentrici o pretenziosamente belli, ma sentivamo la necessità di portare sul palco più popolare d’Italia un messaggio sociale, anche attraverso la moda. L’abito manifesto che da il via alla 73esima edizione del Festival di Sanremo è frutto di una conversazione tra noi, @mariagraziachiuri direttrice artistica di @dior, @racheleregini e Fulvia Carnevale del duo artistico Claire Fontaine @foreignerseverywhere . Il risultato è un abito a corolla di seta nero ispirato alla tradizione @dior e completato dalla stola-manifesto con ricamato il claim “Pensati libera”. Le semplici e pur così forti parole arrivano da una fotografia scattata da Claire Fontaine che speriamo possano ispirare tutte le donne a sentirsi libere di uscire dal ruolo che  è stato a loro imposto dalla società. Una presa di coscienza della stessa Chiara Ferragni che lotta per non essere incasellata in uno spazio identificato per lei dal patriarcato, e anche una promessa che lei stessa si fa ogni giorno mentre lotta per non doversi sentire in colpa del suo successo di donna. “Pensati libera” è dedicato a tutte le donne che hanno voglia di sentirsi semplicemente loro stesse senza essere giudicate.

Il vestito senza vergogna:

Riportare l’attenzione sui diritti delle donne, del loro corpo e su come il disporre del corpo femminile dalle stesse sia, purtroppo, ancora considerato discusso e discutibile. Questo è l’obiettivo dietro questo look. L’idea di un abito che simulasse il corpo nudo di Chiara ci è arrivata immediatamente prendendo ispirazione da una creazione di @mariagraziachiuri per @dior della primavera/estate 2018. Realizzato negli atelier alta moda @dior il vestito in tulle color carne riproduce con un ricamo trompe l'oeil il corpo di @chiaraferragni al naturale e liberato da quella vergogna che hanno sempre imposto a tutte, a partire da Eva, la prima donna della storia indotta a provare vergogna. 

Questa illusione di nudità vuole ricordare a tutte il diritto e l’uguaglianza di genere che hanno nel mostrare, disporre di se stesse senza doversi sentire giudicate o colpevoli. Questa illusione di nudità vuole ricordare che chiunque decida di mostrarsi, o sentirsi sexy non autorizza nessuno a giustificare le violenze degli uomini o ad attenuarne le colpe.

Questo è il corpo di una donna, quello di @chiaraferragni che vorrebbe dare voce a tutte le donne del mondo a cui vengono imposti divieti e abusi, a tutte coloro a cui viene detto che il loro corpo genera vergogna, che è solo un oggetto del desiderio o che istiga al peccato. 

Questo è il corpo di tutte. Chi è senza peccato scagli la prima pietra!

L’abito contro l’odio:

Con questo abito peplo portiamo sul palco del teatro Ariston alcune delle critiche rivolte a Chiara sul suo aspetto, sul suo corpo e soprattutto sulla sua libertà di sentirsi donna oltre che mamma. Le frasi di disprezzo ricamate in perle nere sono le vere offese che ogni giorno gli haters rivolgono alle sue foto postate su Instagram. @mariagraziachiuri ha avuto l’idea di ricamare queste parole NERE su un peplo BIANCO come la pagina di un libro che racconta quel disprezzo infruttifero contro il quale lottare ogni singolo giorno. Portando queste frasi sessiste a @sanremorai vogliamo spronare tutte a fregarsene e ricordare alle donne di non farsi abbattere da chi odia perché sono solo i pareri di chi ci ama a contare veramente.

La donna e madre guerriera

Essere donne senza dover essere considerate solo delle madri. La lotta femminile contro la colpa di voler conciliare tutto è stato il tema che abbiamo chiesto di elaborare a @danielroseberry per questo abito realizzato dalla maison @schiaparelli . La durezza dell’armatura oro scolpita sui seni di Chiara rappresenta una forza che non ha bisogno di imitare quella maschile per essere considerata di pari livello. Mentre la sottoveste di satin è dipinta di blu perché è da sempre il colore associato alla sacralità della maternità qui rappresentata come stereotipo della donna mentre nutre un bambino d’oro. Non essere considerate solo apparati riproduttivi è la scelta per cui combattere ogni singolo giorno!

Body painting

L’impronta oro di un corpo di donna impresso sul blu di un abito a colonna. L’audacia di quel gesto artistico e scandaloso dell’artista Yves Klein ha ispirato il look della ss 2023 di @schiaparelli che secondo @danielroseberry era la sintesi perfetta del nostro progetto sanremese. Nel lavoro dell’artista francese i corpi delle donne erano liberati dalla loro immobilità di manichino e chiamati a imprimere autonomamente le proprie forme su grandi canvas bianchi da dipingere in blu. Liberate il vostro corpo e fatene ciò che volete perché il corpo della donna è il capolavoro massimo della creazione.

L’abito dei diritti umani

Un lungo abito nero di velluto decorato da una collana a forma di utero composta da diverse sezioni di corpo di donna è il simbolo dell’attivismo per i diritti riproduttivi che portiamo a @sanremorai. L’abito e il gioiello disegnati appositamente da @danielroseberry per @schiaparelli ricordano a tutti che i diritti riproduttivi sono diritti umani. Perché l’accesso all’aborto sicuro e alla procreazione assistita è una questione di diritti umani a cui non dobbiamo rinunciare. Perché ogni essere umano, uomo o donna che sia, deve essere messo in grado di prendere liberamente le decisioni sul proprio corpo. Non permettiamo che le lotte vinte dalle nostre madri debbano essere combattute anche dalle nostre figlie.

La femminilità maschile

In molti credono che una donna per essere presa sul serio in certi ambiti debba assumere comportamenti maschili o debba vestirsi da uomo per dimostrare capacità di leadership. L’abito pantalone in velluto nero, interrotto da un corsetto con ricamati di perle a forma di addominali, vuole essere una caricatura a questo stereotipo sessista. Un messaggio agli uomini ancora convinti nella narrazione del “mostrare i muscoli” per essere definite donne degne di rispetto. Non rinunciate alla vostra femminilità perché da qualcuno è considerata un punto di debolezza perché è proprio lì che si trova la forza delle donne.

Brief intermission from the fashion content to talk about my experience with @prenuvo .. January was a month of health for me, and to round it off, I wanted to do the Prenuvo scan so that I had a baseline of health. I’m probably a little bit young to do it but given that I have a couple of health conditions to manage already, I wanted peace of mind. I understand all too well that it is an elective scan that is out of reach for many, but what I want everyone to understand is that they are extremely mission driven company whose long term goal is to democratize health care and make late stage diagnosis a thing of the past. The way they do this is by getting the word out there and getting more funding etc, thus why I’m so happy to talk about it. It takes an hour and you can watch netflix while you do it. Pretty amazing.

Fermarsi a respirare e a pensare, ricordandosi che è normale avere paura, è normale chiedersi se ce la farai, è normale offrire aiuto a chi intorno a te ne ha bisogno ma anche chiederlo a chi sai può esserti di supporto. 
Mi è capitato dopo settimane di cose emotivamente complesse che mi sono successe e ci sono successe come famiglia. 
Sanremo, ora posso ammetterlo, è stato durissima, mi sono sentita fuori dalla mia zona di comfort a chiedermi se sarei stata capace, a dirmi che non potevo deludere chi credeva in me e a non darla vinta a chi mi voleva vedere sbagliare. Che poi certo odio gratuito non capisci proprio perché ti debba essere buttato addosso senza un reale motivo, ma quello è un altro discorso.
Contemporaneamente ho dovuto esserci per la mia famiglia, provare ad essere forte per tutti, a capire come risolvere problemi più grandi di me con la paura di non farcela come moglie e anche come mamma, perché con i tuoi bambini devi essere tu quella forte, sempre. A volte ho provato anche dello sconforto trovandomi a chiedermi cosa sarebbe successo se fossi crollata anche io. Ho pianto, da sola e con chi mi vuole bene e mi ha voluto regalare un abbraccio e una parola di conforto per aiutarmi ad essere forte per tutta la mia famiglia, ma anche per le 60 persone che lavorano con me per cui tutti i giorni devo essere sul pezzo e tener fede agli impegni presi altrimenti restiamo tutti senza lavoro. 
Lo ammetto tutto questo mi ha fatto sentire tra mille fuochi, tra tante, a volte troppe responsabilità familiari, umane e professionali. Ma mi ha fatto trovare anche una nuova forza, forse di persona più adulta. 
Certo a volte vorrei concedermi di dirmi “Chiara ci sei anche tu, oggi puoi essere fragile, puoi sbagliare, puoi essere tu quella che chiede aiuto”. Succederá, lo so. Per ora è il momento di tirare dritto e provare a far funzionare le cose, di aggiustarle senza fingere che tutto vada bene, ma provando a farle andare bene veramente. Grazie a chi c’è anche per me, e a chi capisce che tante volte il mostrarsi forte anche quando ci si sente fragili non è una scelta ma una necessità. Vi vedo, vi leggo e vi sono grata 💖

My earliest memory of Adam Sandler is centered around the movie Little Nicky. In the movie, Nicky has this hilarious voice that is quintessential Sandman. On a long road trip, my little brother and I refused to speak in anything other than the little Nicky voice. I remember my parents begging and pleading to us to use our normal voices but we just couldn’t. We were shrieking with laughter, screaming, “my brother Cassius hit me in the face with a shovel”. When we finally got to our hotel, my parents understandably sent us to bed so that they could go to dinner in peace. We happily sat down to eat our room service and turned on the TV and what happened to be on but little Nicky. (And that was back in the days when there was like five channels). We of course took it as a sign from Adam Sandler himself. 

I love Adam Sandler for a very simple reason: He makes me happy when I’m sad and when I’m already happy, he makes me happier. His movies and his characters still make me laugh the same level of hysterical laugh I had in the back of my parents minivan. 

I’m grateful for all of the laughs he’s given me. I’m grateful for all of his iconic one liners I say in my every day life. And I’m super beyond grateful I got to see my idol win the Mark Twain prize, because watching all of these other comedy greats toast to Adam Sandler was truly a once in a lifetime experience.

There were overarching themes to what everyone had to say about him - what a goof he is, what a genuinely good guy he is, and how much he takes care of his friends and family. What more could you ask for in an idol!! 

Finally, I want to say publicly for the first time that my favorite Sandler movie is Jack & Jill and I am no longer ashamed. May we all be a little more like Adam ❤️

I made my own shoe with Atoms! It’s called 251. The length of my first YouTube video was 2:51, and this feels like a new beginning in the same way 🤓 Everything from the sole to the laces was designed by yours truly. It’s been a 2 year design/build process and I’m so pumped to finally get them out in the world! They ship immediately and link is in bio!
Could’ve, would’ve, should’ve.

The story behind my collaboration with Atoms for a sneaker: I think my favorite video I’ve ever made was when I got to interview Kobe Bryant (during his farewell tour season, in the basement of the Staples Center). I was obviously pretty awestruck, (it was my first interview ever) but I also came away from that super impressed with his approach to creating his own sneakers. He had an incredible amount of input into all of the details of his own signature shoe, and it showed. Turns out that’s pretty rare for a signature shoe athlete.

Fast forward a few years, and when Atoms approached me with their vision for a completely new sneaker, I was immediately intrigued. Now I won’t name names, but I’d actually gotten that pitch before, but it turned out to essentially be a chance to slap my name on something that was almost finished… not interested in that. But Atoms was completely game to start from scratch and create something completely new… I couldn’t say yes fast enough.

This was in 2020, and I was straight off to the drawing board, firing ideas at Atoms designers and experts, and figuring out what could work, what couldn’t, what would cost more, what would cost less, etc. It quickly grew into a deep collaboration between myself and the Atoms team. We shared a passion for design and innovation, and we knew that we could create something truly unique together.

So if you haven’t already, I encourage you to check out the result of the MKBHD x Atoms collaboration. It represents my best ideas as a product enthusiast, and a sneakerhead for a comfortable, versatile, daily wear shoe. It's only available for a limited time, and it's a chance to own something truly special. Thanks for your support, guys, and as always, stay tuned for more!

Pensavo che il momento in cui un’altra cagnolina fosse entrata nella mia vita qualcosa sarebbe cambiato e avrei potuto pensare un pò meno alla mia compagna di 13 anni, Mati. 
Invece è proprio il contrario: ogni suo movimento, profumo e rumore mi riporta alla realtà delle cose: Mati ormai è sulla nuvoletta che i bimbi salutano ogni mattina, e Paloma è la nostra nuova compagna di avventure. 
È un sentimento malinconico quello che provo: è come se di colpo mi fossi resa conto che Mati non è più realmente parte di questa famiglia e mi può guardare con i suoi occhioni solo da lassù, mentre per tutto questo tempo era stata lei la mia certezza contro tutte le cose sbagliate del mondo. 
Si dimenticano tante cose con il tempo ma mai come qualcuno ci ha fatto sentire: sei stata la compagna più vera e piena d’amore che potessi desiderare Mati. 
Spero tu possa ricordarlo sempre da quella nuvoletta lassù. Mi mancherai sempre ed è giusto cosi, perchè un amore del genere non si esaurisce mai.

This weekend I was thinking about my upcoming wedding and how my relationship with my boo has changed over the years. While I’m not usually a super sentimental person, I got incredibly emotional thinking about all the things we’ve faced together. You know him as the guy who occasionally makes a cameo on my IG stories, but to me, G is the guy who loved me before all of this - before the money, before the success, before the endless possibilities. He has always loved me for me. 

6.5 years and thousands of memories later, I know G as the guy who: 
1) Spent $150 on a charity event ticket (I was hosting the event) while eating PB&J’s at his desk at work to save money. 
2) Tried chicken feet at dim sum, not because he wanted to, but because he knew I loved them, and wanted to share the experience. (He did not like lol)
3) Killed cockroaches WITH HIS BARE HANDS in my roach-infested walk-up apartment. (My hero)
4) Planned an elaborate proposal all while working tirelessly at his fancy job to afford my fancy ring (LMFAO)
5) Helped me clean nacho cheese off of my black dress when I got a little too drunk and messy (it was a wedding - sue me)
6) Always runs me TP in 2 minutes or less :)

I know I’ve said it before, but choosing the right partner makes a world of difference, both in your emotional, mental, and physical well-being, but also in your career success and ability to build a financial foundation. I wouldn’t have had the guts to take @your.RichBFF full time without his support, and I hope that everyone reading this already has or gets to find a love that makes you feel like you’re the greatest person on earth, even on your worst days. 

P.S. If you date men, Libra men are amazing. Stay away from Aquariuses. Sorry. I said what I said.

Da tempo volevo diventare donatrice di sangue ed oggi finalmente ho fatto la mia prima donazione 🥹🩸
Un piccolo gesto che però tanto piccolo non è: una singola donazione aiuta come minimo tre pazienti riceventi (ogni sacca viene divisa in plasma, piastrine e globuli rossi) ed il sangue donato aiuta anche la ricerca verso moltissime malattie e patologie.
Donare sangue ha dei vantaggi anche verso il donatore: ad ogni donazione vengono fatti diversi screening di medicina preventiva. 
Si dà per scontato che le strutture ospedaliere abbiano tanto sangue a disposizione ma mi è stato detto che invece spronare la gente a donare è importantissimo perchè c’è sempre più bisogno: se avete sempre voluto farlo e non avete mai provato non abbiate paura, tutto il procedimento è veloce ed assolutamente non doloroso. 
Grazie a tutti i donatori per aver salvato la vita di migliaia di persone, compresa quella di mio marito. 
Sono orgogliosa di esserlo diventata anche io 🥹

Yesterday was one of the saddest days of my life. I lost my Hazel. I can’t believe my girl is gone. My heart hurts so much. It all happened so fast, I’m still in shock. I miss her so much. 

Hazel is the reason behind everything. Without Hazel there would be no Jordan and Dani. There would be no Stella or Stratton. My life wouldn’t be the same. God put that sweet angel in my life for a reason and I KNEW it the moment I laid eyes on her. 

9 years ago, in 2014, I was hired as a model for a fitness commercial at Lake Austin. Upon arrival, I saw the most precious golden retriever puppy bouncing around her owner. As a lover of dogs, I walked up to the owner and asked if I could pet her. That owner was Jordan. That puppy was Hazel. It was love at first sight between me and Hazel. I knew I had to have her in my life. If it took getting close to Jordan, I was going to make it happen!

The next 3 months me and Hazel were inseparable. I was a senior in college about to graduate and had all the time in the world to play with Hazel. We ran Lake Austin every day and somehow she ALWAYS ended up in the water. She loved the water. We’d come back all muddy and stinky, I was like a little kid again. I introduced her to all my friends, we filmed all my youtube videos together, we paddle boarded and swam and hiked and played. We snuggled so hard every night. At the same time, I was getting know Jordan and honestly fell in love with him because of how he treated Hazel. I remember thinking, dang I hope one day a man treats me the same way this guy treats his dog! Hazel was royalty. 

The last 9 years haven’t exactly been easy. Whether I’ve shared it or not online, I’ve been through a lot and I continue to go through a lot. Hazel was there to comfort me through every single moment. Through illness, pregnancies, post partum depression, anxiety, fear, Hazel was with me through it all. I’ll always cherish her for loving me unconditionally. 

Jordan is so incredibly sad. Haven’t seen him like this in a while. I know Hazel was his first love. He is the absolute best dad and I know Hazel played a huge role in that. 

RIP my Hazel girl. You know you’re always my girl. 💔

LONG POST- After the wannabe Baywatch scene in my last video about my pet octopus, I had a good number of people asking what I do for working out. 1) I feel so much of how you build/show muscle is genetics (e.g. If I copied The Rock’s exact workout I will never look like The Rock) so don’t believe the workout programs with 0.1% genetic outliers promising otherwise. 2) I’ve done pushups and situps for 3 minutes before showering nearly everyday of my adult life. It’s a quick, simple habit so engrained now, it feels real unpleasant if have to skip a day. But a few months ago I just started actually working out 2-3x a week at gym to test a theory. Our brains are really good at finding a nice balance between pleasure and suffering. Even if you tried to just live a life of just pleasure it would normalize. This is why drugs stop being great after a while or conversely why nurses can still laugh in a cancer ward. It’s called hedonic adaptation and a really great book called Dopamine Nation dives deep into this topic. So why not proactively seek out the out the suffering moments you’re gonna experience anyways and use them to your advantage?!? That’s the gym for me. But it could also be things like an education, eating at least 1 healthy meal/day, cardio exercise, getting out of your comfort zone for growth or selfless acts as a parent or volunteer when it would be more enjoyable to do what you want to do. It’s a working theory but I’ve found it to be a useful mindset cause while I’m going through the unavoidable suffering I know the activity is benefiting me plus I know my brain owes me some pleasure later to balance things out :)

Ahead of #Spar4Anthony featuring @ksi and @ishowspeed, we want to take a moment to remember Anthony Walker, the heart and soul of the Anthony Walker Foundation (AWF).

While many remember the brutal, racially motivated murder that took Anthony’s life,  The AWF want to take this opportunity to celebrate Anthony’s legacy.
 
Anthony was more than a victim; he was a cherished son, brother, uncle, and a valued community member, known for his humour, kindness, and creativity. His love for basketball is immortalised in the AWF logo, showcasing his silhouette.
 
A devout Christian and enthusiastic youth worker, Anthony dreamt of studying law to become a human rights lawyer. His promising future was cruelly taken on July 30, 2005, in a horrific, racially motivated axe attack, impacting not just the local community but the entire UK.
 
Dr Gee Walker MBE and the Walker family's response was extraordinary. Refusing to let Anthony become just another hate crime statistic, Dr Gee, driven by her faith, expressed forgiveness to her son’s killers and established The AWF. The Foundation aims to combat racism, support racial and religious hate crime victims, and promote harmony through education, sport, and the arts, striving for safer, hate-free communities.
 
To support our charity please donate by visiting:  https://justgiving.com/anthonywalkerfoundation (link in bio)

OR by texting AWF followed by your donation amount to 70490 to give that amount. For example, text AWF5 to donate £5, AWF10 to donate £10, etc. Texts cost the donation amount plus one standard network rate message. Please seek the bill payer’s permission before donating.

I love electric cars, but as I've said on the Auto Focus channel there are certain TYPES of vehicles that with today's tech are BEST when made electric. Take a luxury sedan - what do you want from the best one? It better be super smooth, comfortable, quiet (and probably expensive). A new electric version? Literally the smoothest, quietest, most spacious version ever. (also probably expensive). Total win across the board. 

But sports cars are not one of those things. Yet. The power is there, duh, but there's also a ton of weight that comes with it. And the best sports car across the board rivers best when it's lighter, nimble and reliable. The gap is closing (and hybrids are getting VERY good) out the apex sports car is still not fully electric. 

Honestly I was nervous to get it after watching basically every review on the internet proclaiming this to be the "best car ever created" and "too good" but the professionals were on to something. I'm not ready to say it's the best car ever made, but most of its traits are already top 5% of any car I've ever experienced: Handling, steering feel, balance, physical switches, interior build quality, speakers, acceleration (ok it's 8/10ths as quick as PLAID)

The tech is actually kinda bad compared to new EVs. The backup camera is weak, there's no phone key, the app does almost nothing, no dashcam, wireless CarPlay/Android Auto are welcome but also honestly still not very good. I don't even think that's a hot take.

I've compared smartphones to the Porsche 911's incremental improvement model for years. When the category is young, we call it lazy. When the category is mature, we call it refinement. And I'm only 700 miles in, but damn this car is REFINED as hell.

So this is the new daily 🤓 It's no Carrera GT (♥️ @dougdemuro) but it's MY Turbo S and i love this thing
